adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.8. No events are scheduled, but the price is up 2.3% and the product is trending on TikTok. Past price increases (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show no lift—sales dropped to 10 and 7, respectively—indicating price sensitivity. The TikTok trend is a new driver with no historical precedent; the noise-adjusted effect of similar trends is not available. The classical model suggests a slight downside (x0.98), but this is based only on Halloween’s prior effect, which was muted. No past promotion matches this price or driver. The evidence for a positive lift is weak. Adjust cautiously.

brief:
PRODUCT: School Notebooks 5-pack | category Office | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.8 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 27.2 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 18.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
